questions.question: Which of the following can be used to generate FM phone signals?

choices.A: Balanced modulation of the audio amplifier
choices.B: Reactance modulation of a local oscillator
choices.C: Reactance modulation of the final amplifier
choices.D: Balanced modulation of a local oscillator

questions.answer: Reactance modulation of a local oscillator

questions.question: What is the function of a reactance modulator?

choices.A: Produce PM or FM signals by varying a resistance
choices.B: Produce AM signals by varying an inductance
choices.C: Produce AM signals by varying a resistance
choices.D: Produce PM or FM signals by varying a capacitance

questions.answer: Produce PM or FM signals by varying a capacitance

questions.question: What is a frequency discriminator?

choices.B: A circuit for filtering closely adjacent signals
choices.D: A circuit for detecting FM signals

questions.answer: A circuit for detecting FM signals

questions.question: What is one way to produce a single-sideband phone signal?

choices.A: Use a balanced modulator followed by a filter
choices.B: Use a reactance modulator followed by a mixer
choices.C: Use a loop modulator followed by a mixer
choices.D: Use a product detector with a DSB signal

questions.answer: Use a balanced modulator followed by a filter

questions.question: What is added to an FM speech channel to boost the higher audio frequencies?
Why is de-emphasis used in FM communications receivers?

choices.A: For compatibility with transmitters using phase modulation

questions.answer: For compatibility with transmitters using phase modulation

questions.question: What is meant by the term “baseband” in radio communications?

choices.A: The lowest frequency band that the transmitter or receiver covers
choices.B: The frequency range occupied by a message signal prior to modulation
choices.C: The unmodulated bandwidth of the transmitted signal
choices.D: The basic oscillator frequency in an FM transmitter that is multiplied to increase the deviation and carrier frequency

questions.answer: The frequency range occupied by a message signal prior to modulation

questions.question: What are the principal frequencies that appear at the output of a mixer?

choices.A: Two and four times the input frequency
choices.B: The square root of the product of input frequencies
choices.C: The two input frequencies along with their sum and difference frequencies

questions.answer: The two input frequencies along with their sum and difference frequencies

questions.question: What occurs when the input signal levels to a mixer are too high?

choices.D: Excessive AGC voltage levels are generated

questions.question: How does a diode envelope detector function?

choices.A: By rectification and filtering of RF signals
choices.B: By breakdown of the Zener voltage
choices.C: By mixing signals with noise in the transition region of the diode
choices.D: By sensing the change of reactance in the diode with respect to frequency

questions.answer: By rectification and filtering of RF signals

questions.question: Which type of detector is used for demodulating SSB signals?
What is the modulation index of an FM signal?

choices.A: The ratio of frequency deviation to modulating signal frequency
choices.B: The ratio of modulating signal amplitude to frequency deviation
choices.C: The modulating signal frequency divided by the bandwidth of the transmitted signal
choices.D: The bandwidth of the transmitted signal divided by the modulating signal frequency

questions.answer: The ratio of frequency deviation to modulating signal frequency

questions.question: How does the modulation index of a phase-modulated emission vary with RF carrier frequency?

choices.A: It increases as the RF carrier frequency increases
choices.B: It decreases as the RF carrier frequency increases
choices.C: It varies with the square root of the RF carrier frequency
choices.D: It does not depend on the RF carrier frequency

questions.answer: It does not depend on the RF carrier frequency

questions.question: What is the modulation index of an FM phone signal having a maximum frequency deviation of 3000 Hz either side of the carrier frequency if the highest modulating frequency is 1000 Hz?
What is the modulation index of an FM phone signal having a maximum carrier deviation of plus or minus 6 kHz if the highest modulating frequency is 2 kHz?
What is the deviation ratio of an FM phone signal having a maximum frequency swing of plus or minus 5 kHz if the highest modulation frequency is 3 kHz?
What is the deviation ratio of an FM phone signal having a maximum frequency swing of plus or minus 7.5 kHz if the highest modulation frequency is 3.5 kHz?
Orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) is a technique used for which types of amateur communication?

choices.D: OFDM signals are not allowed on amateur bands

questions.question: What describes orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM)?

choices.A: A frequency modulation technique that uses non-harmonically related frequencies
choices.B: A bandwidth compression technique using Fourier transforms
choices.C: A digital mode for narrow-band, slow-speed transmissions
choices.D: A digital modulation technique using subcarriers at frequencies chosen to avoid intersymbol interference

questions.answer: A digital modulation technique using subcarriers at frequencies chosen to avoid intersymbol interference

questions.question: What is deviation ratio?

choices.A: The ratio of the audio modulating frequency to the center carrier frequency
choices.B: The ratio of the maximum carrier frequency deviation to the highest audio modulating frequency
choices.C: The ratio of the carrier center frequency to the audio modulating frequency
choices.D: The ratio of the highest audio modulating frequency to the average audio modulating frequency

questions.answer: The ratio of the maximum carrier frequency deviation to the highest audio modulating frequency

questions.question: What is frequency division multiplexing (FDM)?

choices.A: The transmitted signal jumps from band to band at a predetermined rate
choices.B: Dividing the transmitted signal into separate frequency bands that each carry a different data stream
choices.C: The transmitted signal is divided into packets of information
choices.D: Two or more information streams are merged into a digital combiner, which then pulse position modulates the transmitter

questions.answer: Dividing the transmitted signal into separate frequency bands that each carry a different data stream

questions.question: What is digital time division multiplexing?

choices.A: Two or more data streams are assigned to discrete sub-carriers on an FM transmitter
choices.B: Two or more signals are arranged to share discrete time slots of a data transmission
choices.C: Two or more data streams share the same channel by transmitting time of transmission as the sub-carrier
choices.D: Two or more signals are quadrature modulated to increase bandwidth efficiency

questions.answer: Two or more signals are arranged to share discrete time slots of a data transmission
